name: SIGMA - Repeated Failed Sign-Ins (Windows Security 4625) [threshold]
description: Elastic threshold companion for rules/sigma/auth_win_bruteforce_failed_logons.yml (issue #192). Alerts when a single target account (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) accrues >=5 Security 4625 failed-logon events within a 5-minute window. The Sigma file is the documented logic-of-record (single-event definition of a failed logon); this threshold rule adds the count that sigma_eval.py / the lucene conversion target cannot express. security-auditor review (#393): the original "from": "now-6m" (a flat +1-minute overlap over the 5-minute "interval") was mathematically incomplete, not just approximate — a real sliding 5-minute window is fully contained in a single 6-minute run window only when its start falls in a 1-minute band out of every 5 (containment probability 1/5 = 20% for an arbitrary-phase campaign; independently verified via the same method #392 used for the SSH cadence rule). Corrected to "from": "now-10m" (lookback >= interval + the 5-minute detection window), which GUARANTEES full containment for any campaign phase, not just improves the odds — any 5-minute-or-wider containment band is guaranteed to contain a multiple of the 5-minute interval. Cost: the effective counting window widens from 6 to 10 minutes (slightly more false-positive-prone at the same threshold.value; not retuned here) and each event is now evaluated by up to 2 consecutive runs instead of ~1.2, which may produce duplicate alerts depending on Kibana Detection Engine's own alert-deduplication behavior — not independently verified against multiple real scheduled runs in this change (see tests/detections/test_live_fire.py's ThresholdLiveFireTests for the aggregation-correctness proof this change does carry).
author: Suburban-SOC
false_positives: High-volume legitimate failures during a mass password-reset rollout.
Load-balanced authentication proxies retrying with stale credentials.
